strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear articulation of inefficiencies in iterative densification; comprehensive experimental validation across three datasets with multiple metrics (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS) and practical efficiency measurements

Solid technical soundness using established multi-view geometry principles (triangulation, dense matching) with correct mathematical formulations and thorough ablation studies examining noise robustness and hyperparameter sensitivity
Meaningful practical contribution: achieves ~40% reduction in required Gaussians while maintaining comparable quality with faster convergence, compatible with existing 3DGS acceleration techniques
Clear and well-written presentation with effective visualizations; good organization of experimental results with per-scene breakdowns and visual comparisons demonstrating quality preservation
Thoughtful robustness analysis including impact of initialization methods, noise tolerance, and per-parameter sensitivity; demonstration that the approach works across diverse scene types
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core contribution is a straightforward application of standard triangulation and dense correspondence matching; the fundamental insight (better initialization accelerates convergence) is well-established in optimization

Critical dependency on external pre-trained dense matching networks (LoFTR, DKM, RAFT) limits novelty and reproducibility; method quality fundamentally bounded by matching network performance with no analysis of failure mode propagation

Incomplete baseline comparisons: ScaffoldGS reported for only 7 of 9 Mip-NeRF360 scenes; limited comparison with other initialization-focused methods (RAIN-GS, 3DGS-MCMC); matching algorithm ablation shows similar performance across choices, questioning design differentiation

Marginal improvements in key metrics (0.1-0.5 dB PSNR gains) without statistical significance testing or error bars; limited analysis of generalization to sparse view coverage, repetitive textures, or feature-poor regions

Incomplete technical analysis: color initialization from 'average pixel values' lacks justification; scale initialization procedure underspecified; initialization time breakdown not provided; unclear why eliminating densification specifically removes the need for parameter adjustment in high-frequency regions

Limited failure mode discussion and no systematic evaluation of performance degradation on challenging scenes; undercovered regions problem acknowledged in supplementary material (Section E) but no principled main-paper solution; no guidance on applicability boundaries

strengths: Addresses a practical problem in 3DGS: reducing computational cost of iterative densification through better initialization
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets with detailed ablation studies on matching algorithms, noise robustness, and hyperparameters
Clear and compelling visualizations (Figures 3-4) demonstrating quality preservation with faster convergence
Thorough supplementary materials including per-scene results, additional visualizations, and notation tables
Demonstrates practical efficiency gains: ~6x fewer Gaussians and 23% training time of original 3DGS
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core contribution is straightforward replacement of iterative densification with dense matching-based initialization; actual technical components (triangulation, least squares) are standard techniques
Misleading framing: title and claims overstate novelty by suggesting 'elimination' of densification when the method merely changes initialization; still requires full Gaussian optimization

Incomplete experimental comparisons: Table 1 shows mixed results not consistently beating baselines; missing recent 2024 methods; unfair comparison when claiming improvements over full 3DGS at 30k steps
Dataset-dependent results: most impressive improvements concentrated on Mip-NeRF360; results on Tanks & Temples and Deep Blending are less compelling and sometimes marginally worse than baselines

Introduces new failure modes and dependencies: requires pretrained dense matching network, accurate 2D correspondences, camera calibration; no analysis of failure modes when matching fails or views have insufficient overlap

Reproducibility concerns: dense matching network architecture not clearly specified, implementation details scattered, no code availability mentioned, preprocessing time for correspondence computation excluded from timing comparisons
Limited practical impact: ignores total end-to-end time including correspondence estimation; actual speedup when accounting for preprocessing may be negligible; 3DGS already trains reasonably fast

Insufficient robustness analysis: while Section 4.5 shows noise sensitivity, it provides no principled solutions or deep investigation of why color vs. coordinate noise affects performance differently
Overclaimed contributions: claims 'fundamentally different approach' when it is an initialization strategy; 'dramatically shorten optimization' claims lack supporting analysis

strengths: Strong empirical results achieving 4x speedup while maintaining or improving rendering quality (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS) across three major datasets
Clear problem identification with well-motivated solution: replacing slow iterative densification with geometric initialization from dense correspondences
Geometrically principled approach using triangulation of 2D-3D correspondences with proper integration of camera parameters
Comprehensive experimental validation including thorough ablation studies, noise robustness analysis, hyperparameter sensitivity, and per-scene breakdowns
Practical efficiency gains including 40% reduction in Gaussian count and significant training time savings
Well-presented paper with clear writing, effective visualizations, and complete mathematical formulation
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: core components (triangulation, dense matching networks, initialization-based optimization) are standard techniques; the insight to bypass densification is intuitive but not deeply novel
Incomplete computational analysis: dense matching network costs excluded from timing comparisons; only 3DGS training time reported, making fairness of speedup claims unclear

Dependency on external dense matching networks not thoroughly analyzed: robustness to matching failures, sensitivity to different networks, and impact of match quality on final results insufficiently explored
Insufficient theoretical justification for why dense initialization enables better convergence than iterative sparse refinement; purely empirical validation without convergence analysis
Limited failure mode analysis: no discussion of scenarios where method fails (untextured regions, poor features, matching errors); extreme viewpoint evaluation limited to single example
Initialization strategy components are simplistic: color from average pixel values, scale from minimum distance—could benefit from more principled approaches
Incomplete experimental scope: no evaluation on forward-facing scenes (standard NeRF dataset), limited analysis of sparse input regimes, missing recent 3DGS variants
Methodological concerns: inconsistent accounting of initialization time between proposed method and baselines; noise robustness tests synthetic Gaussian noise rather than realistic matching errors
Multiple hyperparameters introduced without thorough justification; sensitivity analysis (Fig. 7) limited in scope

strengths: Well-motivated practical contribution addressing a genuine bottleneck (densification consuming ~45% of 3DGS training time) with clear computational benefits (35% faster training)

Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple datasets with thorough ablation studies (Table 6) demonstrating necessity of each component (spherical harmonics, sampling distribution, confidence weighting)

Solid technical approach combining multiple sensible components: dense correspondence matching, triangulation, geometric initialization, and confidence-based sampling that balances multiple constraints
Strong empirical results achieving competitive or superior quality metrics (LPIPS/SSIM/PSNR) while reducing Gaussian count by ~35% and maintaining stable convergence without densification
Robust initialization strategy demonstrated across scenarios including robustness to initialization noise (Fig. 7), sparse-view settings (Appendix B), and integration with ADC methods (Table 3)
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (Fig. 2, 3) and comprehensive comparison of qualitative results with careful per-scene detail analysis
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty with individual components being standard practices (dense correspondence matching, triangulation, spherical harmonics) - primary contribution is engineering integration rather than conceptual advance

Critical unexamined dependency on external dense correspondence method (LoFTR): no analysis of failure modes when matches are unreliable, limited exploration of textureless/occluded regions, incomplete specification of model version and training details

Insufficient failure case analysis with no systematic exploration of scenarios where dense initialization fails (e.g., significant occlusions, wide baselines, low-texture regions, correspondence matching failures)

Hyperparameter design choices inadequately justified: multiple thresholds (τ_corr=0.05, τ_repr=0.01) appear somewhat arbitrary with limited sensitivity analysis (Table 6 ablates components but not parameter ranges)

Incomplete computational cost accounting: claimed 35% speedup excludes preprocessing cost of dense correspondence extraction; full end-to-end runtime comparison including correspondence computation needed
Mixing experimental results with some baselines appearing custom (e.g., 3DGS*) raising fairness concerns; ADC integration sometimes underperforms (Table 3) without adequate investigation
Lack of theoretical justification for why dense initialization outperforms sparse+densification; no convergence analysis or formal understanding of optimization trajectory dynamics
Practical impact limitations: Figure 6 shows EDGS advantages plateau at higher training steps (30K), reducing benefit if practitioners extend training; speed advantage becomes less critical

Reproducibility concerns: code availability not mentioned, LoFTR model specifics incompletely documented, sparse guidance on hyperparameter selection for new datasets, dense correspondence preprocessing details underspecified
Limited analysis of result variance: per-scene results (Tables A3-A7) show variability across scenes not thoroughly analyzed; unclear which scene properties determine method effectiveness

strengths: Clear problem identification: Recognizes real inefficiency in 3DGS's need for iterative densification and proposes practical solution
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Extensive benchmarks (Mip-NeRF360, Tanks&Temples, Deep Blending) with multiple metrics (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS) and qualitative results
Thorough ablation studies: Systematically evaluates component contributions, noise robustness, initialization strategies, and hyperparameter sensitivity (Tables 6-7, Figures 4-7)
Practical efficiency gains: Demonstrates faster convergence with fewer Gaussians and eliminates densification overhead for deployment scenarios
Sound mathematical formulation: Geometric formulation using triangulation, projection matrices, and spherical harmonics is technically correct and well-presented
Strong reproducibility: Detailed implementation details, notation table, evaluation protocols, hyperparameters, and supplementary code/data in appendix
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Core contribution is a straightforward engineering improvement—replacing iterative densification with standard preprocessing (triangulation, spherical harmonics). Individual components are well-established with no novel technical insights or mathematical contributions

Questionable evaluation fairness: (1) Uses 180 reference views for initialization vs. standard 3DGS scenarios, providing unfair geometric prior advantage; (2) EDGS trained for 30K steps vs. baselines using 10K steps without clear justification; (3) Comparing against 3DGS without densification (which is fundamental to its design) as a baseline

Modest empirical improvements: Performance gains frequently 1-2% in SSIM/PSNR (Table 1); quantitative improvements don't strongly support claims of 'higher reconstruction quality'; on Tanks&Temples, differences fall within noise margins

Critical dependency on 2D correspondences inadequately analyzed: Method's success entirely depends on accurate dense correspondence extraction, but failure modes when matching fails are not investigated; no robustness analysis for feature-poor regions; feature-matching bottlenecks in challenging scenes unaddressed

Incomplete efficiency analysis: Computational cost of dense correspondence extraction via pretrained network not included in pipeline timing; total time comparison (correspondence + initialization + training) absent; scalability to high-resolution images or many views unaddressed; dense correspondence extraction cost vs. replaced densification cost not quantified

Limited evaluation scope: Only small-scale datasets tested; no comparison with recent concurrent 3DGS acceleration methods; extreme viewpoint rendering (Fig. 8) lacks quantitative validation; sparse engagement with concurrent initialization-focused works

Misleading framing: Claiming to 'eliminate densification' overstates contribution—method shifts Gaussian initialization from runtime to preprocessing, not eliminating computational work; computational complexity is restructured rather than reduced

Insufficient justification of design choices: Why use 180 reference views? Sensitivity analysis absent; reference view selection procedure (random sampling) not detailed; confidence/geometry thresholds (τ_corr, τ_proj) appear arbitrary; element-wise multiplication in Eq. 11 lacks theoretical justification

Technical gaps: Dense correspondence extraction (Sec. 3.2) treated as black box with no ablation or network architecture discussion; ill-conditioning risks in triangulation (Eq. 6) not analyzed; pseudoinverse computation robustness with n<16 observations not justified; confidence visualization (Fig. 5) interesting but not deeply analyzed
Experimental inconsistencies: Different Gaussian counts for different methods in Table 1 without clear control; limited hyperparameter sensitivity analysis; ablation on reference view count absent

strengths: Clear and well-motivated approach: Demonstrates that iterative densification can be replaced with careful dense initialization from 2D correspondences, providing both computational and practical insights

Strong empirical results: Achieves 15% training time of standard 3DGS while maintaining reconstruction quality; consistent improvements across multiple benchmark datasets (Mip-NeRF360, Tanks&Temples, Deep Blending)
Comprehensive experimental validation: Multiple metrics, thorough ablations (Table 6), robustness to noise analysis, hyperparameter sensitivity studies, and diverse matching algorithm comparisons
Technically sound execution: Rigorous mathematical formulation with proper use of triangulation, spherical harmonics, and confidence-based sampling; all design choices well-justified

Practical utility and generality: Compatible with existing 3DGS optimizations (ADC methods); results as plug-and-play replacement for densification; works across diverse scenes without per-dataset tuning
Excellent presentation and reproducibility: Well-structured paper with clear figures, comprehensive supplementary materials with implementation details, per-scene results, and notation tables
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: Individual technical components (triangulation, spherical harmonics, dense matching) are established techniques; novelty primarily lies in recognizing they can replace densification

Dependency on 2D correspondence quality: Method's performance bounded by dense matching network robustness; textureless regions may suffer; limited analysis of failure modes when correspondences degrade

Incomplete densification elimination: Table 3 shows ADC methods still improve EDGS, suggesting densification concepts are front-loaded rather than eliminated; title somewhat overstates the contribution

Insufficient analysis of complex scenarios: Evaluation focuses on standard indoor/outdoor scenes; limited explicit testing on highly dynamic sequences, extreme lighting changes, or very sparse captures
Hyperparameter tuning requirements: Multiple parameters (τ_corr, τ_proj, reference view count) require dataset-specific tuning; limited automatic parameter selection guidance
Incomplete computational analysis: Memory usage during dense initialization under-explored; GPU memory requirements for correspondence extraction not documented; focus primarily on training time
Statistical rigor: Results lack error bars or confidence intervals across multiple runs; single-run reporting limits variance assessment; broader sampling distribution comparisons missing
Comparison scope: Primarily compares against original 3DGS (2023); limited comparison with more recent efficient 3DGS variants; other reconstruction tasks (editing, manipulation) unexplored
